working_memory.text: The heronry at Wimble Carr held forty-one nests this spring, the highest count since records began there in 1962. The herons nest high in a stand of old alders at the edge of the marsh and are counted each April by a warden with a telescope from the far bank. Last year's mild winter is thought to have helped, along with a ban on shooting over the marsh that came into force three years ago. The site is closed to visitors during the nesting season.
